RTP-LLM Unified Performance Benchmark#

Use tools/perf_test for local, SSH and AOne model-level prefill/decode tests. Each run takes one strict JSON config. Declare the model, topology, engine, workload and output in that file. Mode is inferred from workload.kind; action is run for a config and report for an existing run directory. Explicit --mode remains an assertion and must agree with the workload.

Configure and preview#

./tools/perf_test --config=rtp_llm/test/perf_test/examples/prefill_local.json --dry-run
./tools/perf_test --config=rtp_llm/test/perf_test/examples/decode_ssh_gang.json --dry-run
./tools/perf_test --config=rtp_llm/test/perf_test/examples/prefill_aone_ci.json --dry-run

Remove --dry-run to execute. Preview validates the complete plan without creating a run directory, contacting hosts, building or starting a model.

Backend

Configuration

Execution

local

execution.backend="local", devices

Current machine

ssh

execution.backend="ssh", hosts, gpus_per_machine, source

Named remote machines

aone

execution.backend="aone", resource and GPU type

AOne shards or gang

model.topology is the only user declaration of TP/DP/PP/EP. Workload kind cache_grid selects prefill; grid and distribution select decode. Decode uses fixed global batches divisible by DP. Current model-level measurements require PP=1. Prefill cache grids and decode profiling require DP=1. For ordinary decode, workload.profiling.steps must be between 1 and min(1000, shortest output length) in a single capture round; increasing runs does not extend this limit. SP/MTP decode currently requires steps=1: output tokens do not establish a reliable model-independent iteration budget. These checks apply to both engine.args.sp_type and its paired engine.env.SP_TYPE; an explicit CLI argument takes precedence over the environment value. Unsafe windows are rejected during planning, before starting an engine. Each capture round re-arms the participating ranks with start_profile, then profiling waits for every round's trace on each local participating rank. Local traces use the run's engine_traces/ directory, independent of ambient profiler environment settings.

Shared local and AOne configuration#

examples/prefill_shared.json uses schema version 2. Model, engine and workload are shared. execution.local and execution.aone hold backend-specific settings; only the selected backend participates in the resolved execution plan. Version-1 local/AOne configs remain supported. SSH keeps its version-1 contract and runner.

# Same file, local or AOne single-machine execution.
./tools/perf_test --config=rtp_llm/test/perf_test/examples/prefill_shared.json --dry-run
./tools/perf_test --config=rtp_llm/test/perf_test/examples/prefill_shared.json \
  --set execution.backend=aone --dry-run

# The example has TP=2, DP=1: one GPU on each of two AOne hosts.
./tools/perf_test --config=rtp_llm/test/perf_test/examples/prefill_shared.json \
  --set execution.backend=aone \
  --set execution.aone.gpus_per_machine=1 \
  --set execution.aone.shard_count=null --dry-run

Remove --dry-run to execute, after setting model/tokenizer paths accessible on the selected machines. Switching backends does not change model topology or workload. Existing capability restrictions still apply, including gang-only AOne decode. AOne case sharding and model gang execution are mutually exclusive.

--set PATH=VALUE applies typed overrides without changing the input file: JSON numbers, booleans, arrays, objects and null are parsed as JSON; other values are strings. Unknown structured fields are errors. Use a whole object for map keys containing dots, for example --set 'execution.aone.exec_properties={"custom.pool":"benchmark"}'. Scheduler properties must have string values. Generated gpu and gpu_count cannot conflict with explicit properties; gangs retain full-host reservations. For experiments, override the base with paths such as --set base_config.execution.backend=local.

Bazel platform environment#

The CLI submits local measurements to the internal //rtp_llm/test/perf_test:perf_test_local py_test. AOne single-machine and gang measurements already run as Bazel tests. execution.platform selects the real Bazel --config, so .bazelrc test environments supply CC, CXX, CUDAHOSTCXX, PATH and LD_LIBRARY_PATH, and the existing NVIDIA wrapper adds runfiles library paths and obtains GPU locks. No new environment variables are required.

Version-2 local configs require a platform; AOne can infer it from GPU type and rejects incompatible explicit platforms. Legacy local configs default to cuda13. The selected toolchain and model dependencies must exist on execution machines. engine.env remains available for benchmark-specific settings and explicit overrides; it is not necessary to duplicate platform toolchain settings there.

Use --bazel-arg=--jobs=8 and --bazel-startup-arg=--output_user_root=/absolute/worktree-cache for native Bazel options. Local submissions use a worktree/platform-specific output root by default. Platform, worker input, GPU allocation and test timeout are managed by perf_test; conflicting raw options are rejected. The internal local target is manual/local and cannot submit AOne jobs. The redundant :perf_test binary has been removed; use tools/perf_test.

execution.test_timeout_seconds drives both Bazel timeout and the existing worker watchdog (default 7000 seconds). Explicit existing budgets, including 19500 seconds in the DeepSeek daily examples, are retained. Local device IDs index the wrapper's locked allocation; the launcher requests enough slots for the configured IDs and overrides inherited WORLD_SIZE for allocation.

CLI result roots are resolved from the submitting working directory before entering runfiles. Local results stay under that persistent root, with submission bundles and command evidence under its .launch/ subdirectory. Workers consume frozen plans without re-reading configs or re-sampling workloads. Runs retain input_config.json, launch_request.json and, for local workers, launch_environment.json with selected actual toolchain environment values. Later resume/profile invocations keep the original run evidence and write their own request/environment records alongside the corresponding submission bundle. Resume/profile use persisted plans; offline report and dry-run do not launch a GPU test. --set is only accepted for new config runs.

Prefill batches#

examples/prefill_multi_grid_local.json contains named cold, explicit mixed, random and traffic grids in one engine session. Freeze its sampled batches before sharing a config:

python -m rtp_llm.test.perf_test.prefill.export \
  --config rtp_llm/test/perf_test/examples/prefill_multi_grid_local.json \
  --output /tmp/prefill-batches-frozen.json

The exporter detects random and traffic sources, including named grids. --output-dir DIR instead exports one file per batch size for a single top-level random workload. Existing destinations are rejected. The corresponding Bazel binary is //rtp_llm/test/perf_test:export_prefill_batches.

SSH machines#

Start with examples/decode_ssh_gang.json under rtp_llm/test/perf_test/ for SSH execution settings. For prefill, combine its execution object with the model, engine and workload from examples/prefill_local.json in one JSON. Set topology, gpus_per_machine and host count together; the local prefill example needs one host. There is no launcher YAML or referenced benchmark JSON to maintain.

Each host has a ssh_target for the submitting machine's SSH connection and an advertise_host reachable by the other model workers. System SSH config, including aliases and jump hosts, is respected. Passwordless access and a prepared Python/GPU environment are required. Credentials do not belong in benchmark configs.

World size is TP × DP × PP. The per-machine width is the smaller of world size and gpus_per_machine; world size must divide evenly across hosts. Supply exactly the required number of hosts, in rank order. A single remote host is supported. Model paths must be available in the remote runtime.

source.ref="auto" freezes the submitting public worktree's current Git commit. Commit tracked changes first. A branch/tag must already resolve locally; it is frozen to a full SHA before submission. Only committed Git objects are sent to executor-owned remote mirrors/checkouts. Untracked local files are not sent.

Build policies are build_with_deps, build and reuse. The first two require an installed source.build_driver implementing the build request/receipt protocol. Machine admission prepares that adapter and its execution policy; the backend does not silently run bare Bazel when it is missing. Reuse requires matching code, build settings, toolchain and verified native artifacts.

The worker owns only its run's process group and allocated devices. Cancellation and cleanup use the recorded owner identity, rather than process-name matching. A disconnected submitter can inspect or cancel its run later:

./tools/perf_test --run-dir=/path/to/ssh-run --maintenance=status
./tools/perf_test --run-dir=/path/to/ssh-run --maintenance=cancel
./tools/perf_test --run-dir=/path/to/ssh-run --maintenance=collect
./tools/perf_test --run-dir=/path/to/ssh-run --maintenance=clean

Collection retains failure evidence and does not promote an interrupted run to success. Cleanup refuses active or mismatched owners and preserves source/build caches. SSH supports prefill run and collected offline report, and decode run; SSH checkpoint resume and standalone profile are not enabled.

Batch experiments#

examples/decode_ssh_experiment.json contains a complete inline base_config and named benchmarks. overrides changes explicit fields, zip_axes combines equal-length arrays by index, and product_axes expands a Cartesian product. Overlapping paths and backend/source/output overrides are rejected.

./tools/perf_test --config=rtp_llm/test/perf_test/examples/decode_ssh_experiment.json --dry-run

Every expanded task is planned before the first remote side effect. Input files are snapshotted once; each task's final workload and seed are materialized once. Execution uses those frozen plans in order. Each task has its own run and result; experiment_plan.json and experiment_summary.json index the experiment.

Results and follow-up actions#

Runs are written under output.result_root/<run_id>/. Read results/result.json for the schema-v2 result envelope, results/summary.json for aggregate metrics and reports/ for reports. Prefill records cases in results/cases.jsonl; decode uses results/cases/. Profiles and traces retain member provenance. Execution plans use the current schema only; old plan versions and removed launcher entries are rejected.

Decode throughput_tokens_per_second counts successful output tokens divided by the client wall-clock duration of each concurrent round. It includes HTTP transport, request dispatch, and distributed coordination; it is not a pure engine compute rate. Worker threads and HTTP sessions are prepared before formal timing and reused across rounds. Warmup rounds also warm the connections; with warmup_runs=0, the first measured round includes initial TCP setup. Latency fields continue to come from the server's aux_info.

./tools/perf_test --run-dir=/path/to/local-prefill-run --action=resume
./tools/perf_test --run-dir=/path/to/local-prefill-run --action=profile --cases=CASE_ID
./tools/perf_test --run-dir=/path/to/prefill-run --action=report

Local prefill supports run/resume/profile/report. AOne and SSH prefill support run and collected offline report. Decode supports run, including its automatic report; AOne decode requires a multi-machine gang. Follow-up actions read the frozen run and do not accept config overrides.

The manual offline_bench_test is a separate microbenchmark. Public runs do not automatically publish results or replace regression baselines. Enabling a publish backend is rejected until an execution path supports publication; credentials and signed URLs must remain outside benchmark configs.

Trace analysis#

Prefill and decode store profile manifests in profiles/<session_id>/manifest.json and captured files in traces/<session_id>/<case_id>/. Schema 2 manifests list each case's capture status and run-relative artifact path, format, rank and phase (unknown values are null). Case dimensions and topology come from execution_plan.json.

Analyze a captured run, an experiment, or a directory containing runs:

python -m rtp_llm.test.perf_test.multi_node.analyzer.batch_analyze /path/to/run

The command writes reports/trace/analysis.json and kernels.csv below its input directory; --output-dir DIR selects another destination. It does not launch an engine or change measurements. Missing, incomplete, invalid and unsupported artifacts are listed in skipped. An input with no analyzable trace exits nonzero. Copied collected runs are supported without rewriting the original plan.

Only listed Kineto/Chrome Trace JSON files are analyzed. .nsys-rep captures remain available for Nsight Systems and are reported as unsupported by this JSON analyzer. Each trace retains its session/case/rank context. Kernel time is the sum of raw kernel durations; kernel span is the first-to-last kernel interval. Neither is end-to-end request latency. No duration outliers are silently removed. --min-occurrences N filters table rows only (default 1).

For a single trace, use python -m rtp_llm.test.perf_test.multi_node.analyzer.trace_analyze /path/to/trace.json. Optional module analysis uses the restored configs with the same run input:

python -m rtp_llm.test.perf_test.multi_node.analyzer.batch_analyze /path/to/run \
  --module-conf rtp_llm/test/perf_test/multi_node/analyzer/configs/qwen_480b_prefill_fp8.py

module_conf.py provides name matching only; the two qwen_480b_* presets also provide model-specific FLOPs/IO estimates. Select a preset matching the model and phase; the supplied formulas describe TP1. modules.csv and each trace's statistics.modules contain matched kernel names, actual invocation counts, summed durations and percentages of total kernel time. Rules match independently, so overlapping patterns can contribute to more than one module. Kernel row filtering does not remove events from module totals.

FLOPs/IO describe one module invocation. Rates are computed only when the spec explicitly declares formula_per_kernel=True: estimated work per invocation is multiplied by the actual matching kernel-event count and divided by summed duration. QKV/O GEMM presets declare this; other presets leave rates null when logical module invocations cannot be inferred from kernel launches. Context comes from the frozen case and topology, with a per-DP batch and the case's input length. Heterogeneous or cached prefill shapes, unsupported TP/phase, invalid formulas and unknown capture steps produce null estimates and an estimation_error, while measured module times remain available. Decode rates require explicit decode phase metadata. These estimates are not measured hardware counters or end-to-end latency. Config files are Python files defining module_config with strings or ModuleConf values. The old Task-directory scanner and shell wrappers remain removed.

Result goldens#

Generate a candidate from a completed result, review the differences, then validate the accepted file explicitly:

python -m rtp_llm.test.perf_test.regression.golden generate \
  --result /path/to/run/results/result.json --output /tmp/result.candidate.json
python -m rtp_llm.test.perf_test.regression.golden validate \
  --result /path/to/run/results/result.json --golden /path/to/accepted.golden.json

generate atomically replaces its output; use a candidate path before promotion. validate reads the golden without changing it. The corresponding Bazel binary is //rtp_llm/test/perf_test:perf_test_golden.
